Vulnerabilities.Title: apt: apt: Remote code execution via hard link reuse during package download retries
Vulnerabilities.Description:
On Debian, Ubuntu, and derivative Linux distributions, an on-path attacker who can manipulate the HTTP traffic (including a malicious mirror or proxy) between an APT client and an archive server triggered by a package install can trick the client into installing an attacker-controlled unverified package and achieve remote code execution with root privileges.



The vulnerability is caused by the reuse of hard links and requires the client to follow redirects and retry the download of package files. It requires the client to have a non-zero Acquire::Retries configuration setting; the value 3 is the default starting with Debian 12 (bookworm) and Ubuntu 22.04 LTS (Jammy Jellyfish), so older releases are unaffected in a default configuration

Vulnerabilities.Title: It was found that apt-key in apt, all versions, do not correctly valid ...
Vulnerabilities.Description: It was found that apt-key in apt, all versions, do not correctly validate gpg keys with the master keyring, leading to a potential man-in-the-middle attack.

Vulnerabilities.Title: [Privilege escalation possible to other user than root]
util-linux: util-linux: failed external mount helper still runs privileged X-mount post-hooks
Vulnerabilities.Description: util-linux versions through 2.41.5 and 2.42.2 fail to check mount helper exit status before running post-mount hooks, allowing unprivileged users to execute privileged operations on pre-existing filesystems. Attackers can exploit X-mount.idmap or X-mount.owner hooks to clone filesystems with inherited suid bits or modify target inode permissions after a helper fails, achieving privilege escalation.

Vulnerabilities.Title: util-linux: util-linux: nsenter --join-cgroup leaks root cgroup migration authority
Vulnerabilities.Description: The nsenter --join-cgroup option opens the target cgroup.procs file as root and leaves that file descriptor open across later namespace and credential changes and across execve(). Because the kernel checks later cgroup migrations using the credentials from the original open, a program run in an attacker-controlled target can inherit root's ability to move host processes between cgroups. After a privileged operator uses --join-cgroup against that target, an unprivileged user can migrate and terminate unrelated root processes.

Vulnerabilities.Title: util-linux: util-linux: X-mount.subdir detached-tree resolution can escape via intermediate symlinks
Vulnerabilities.Description: The X-mount.subdir option uses a detached-tree fast path on Linux 6.15 and later and passes the configured subdirectory to open_tree() with AT_SYMLINK_NOFOLLOW. That flag does not stop intermediate symlink traversal or keep resolution inside the newly mounted filesystem. A local unprivileged user with an fstab-authorized X-mount.subdir entry can attach a host path at the intended mountpoint.

Vulnerabilities.Title: util-linux: util-linux: restricted bind mounts do not pin the source, allowing X-mount.owner/group/mode redirection
Vulnerabilities.Description: A flaw was found in util-linux. Restricted bind mounts take the source path from fstab but do not pin that source before the privileged mount. A local unprivileged user who can replace the authorized source or a writable ancestor can redirect SUID mount(8) to bind another host directory. If the fstab entry also sets X-mount.owner, X-mount.group, or X-mount.mode, root then changes ownership or mode on that redirected inode.

Vulnerabilities.Title: util-linux: util-linux: Access control bypass due to improper hostname canonicalization
Vulnerabilities.Description: A flaw was found in util-linux. Improper hostname canonicalization in the `login(1)` utility, when invoked with the `-h` option, can modify the supplied remote hostname before setting `PAM_RHOST`. A remote attacker could exploit this by providing a specially crafted hostname, potentially bypassing host-based Pluggable Authentication Modules (PAM) access control rules that rely on fully qualified domain names. This could lead to unauthorized access.

Vulnerabilities.Title: util-linux: partial disclosure of arbitrary files in chfn and chsh when compiled with libreadline
Vulnerabilities.Description: A flaw was found in the util-linux chfn and chsh utilities when compiled with Readline support. The Readline library uses an "INPUTRC" environment variable to get a path to the library config file. When the library cannot parse the specified file, it prints an error message containing data from the file. This flaw allows an unprivileged user to read root-owned files, potentially leading to privilege escalation. This flaw affects util-linux versions prior to 2.37.4.

Vulnerabilities.Title: coreutils: race condition vulnerability in chown and chgrp
Vulnerabilities.Description: In GNU Coreutils through 8.29, chown-core.c in chown and chgrp does not prevent replacement of a plain file with a symlink during use of the POSIX "-R -L" options, which allows local users to modify the ownership of arbitrary files by leveraging a race condition.

Vulnerabilities.Title: coreutils: Heap Buffer Under-Read in GNU Coreutils sort via Key Specification
Vulnerabilities.Description: A flaw was found in GNU Coreutils. The sort utility's begfield() function is vulnerable to a heap buffer under-read. The program may access memory outside the allocated buffer if a user runs a crafted command using the traditional key format. A malicious input could lead to a crash or leak sensitive data.

Vulnerabilities.Title: coreutils: GNU coreutils uniq: Denial of Service and information disclosure via out-of-bounds read with multibyte input
Vulnerabilities.Description:
GNU coreutils uniq is vulnerable to an out‑of‑bounds read due to incorrect handling of multibyte input when the -w (--check-chars) option is used. The find_field() function miscalculates the byte length of characters by repeatedly processing a fixed pointer instead of advancing through the input, resulting in an inflated length value. 
This incorrect length is later used in a memcmp operation, causing reads beyond the allocated buffer when processing crafted multibyte input.

When running GNU coreutils uniq with attacker-provided arguments, this behavior leads to a crash and potential adjacent heap memory exposure.


This issue has been fixed in the commit d64e35a8a4c0e4608321433e0d84d917e4e36371.

Vulnerabilities.Title: coreutils: GNU coreutils unexpand: Denial of Service via crafted tab stop values
Vulnerabilities.Description:
GNU coreutils unexpand is vulnerable to a heap-based buffer overflow due to an integer overflow during buffer allocation when processing large tab stop (-t) values. The multiplication used to calculate the allocation size can wrap around, resulting in an undersized buffer.
When processing crafted input, subsequent writes exceed the allocated memory, leading to an out‑of‑bounds heap write.

When running GNU coreutils unexpand with attacker-provided large tab stop (-t) arguments, this behavior leads to a crash and potentially achieve a heap write primitive depending on memory layout.










This issue has been fixed in the commit b60a159fdc5bfcf9988d3a4cb6f53abe8ad5d35d

Vulnerabilities.Title: curl: curl: SSH host verification bypass when using schemeless URLs with SFTP/SCP
Vulnerabilities.Description:
When a user invokes curl using a schemeless URL combined with
`--proto-default` sftp (or scp), a disconnect occurs between the tool layer
and libcurl. The tool layer incorrectly infers the URL scheme, which
erroneously bypasses the initialization of critical SSH security options like
CURLOPT_SSH_HOST_PUBLIC_KEY_SHA256 and CURLOPT_SSH_KNOWNHOSTS. Conversely, the
libcurl runtime successfully honors CURLOPT_DEFAULT_PROTOCOL and establishes
the connection via SFTP/SCP as specified. Because the tool layer skipped the
security configuration, these SSH host verification options are silently
omitted, causing curl to connect to an unverified SSH remote host without
throwing an error.

Vulnerabilities.Title: curl: libcurl: Unauthorized connection reuse due to a logical error
Vulnerabilities.Description:
libcurl might in some circumstances reuse the wrong connection when asked to
do Negotiate-authenticated ones, even when they are set to use different
"services".

libcurl features a pool of recent connections so that subsequent requests can
reuse an existing connection to avoid overhead.

When reusing a connection a range of criteria must be met. Due to a logical
error in the code, a request that was issued by an application could
wrongfully reuse an existing connection to the same server that was
authenticated using different services.

Vulnerabilities.Title: libcurl: libcurl: Use-after-free vulnerability leading to Denial of Service
Vulnerabilities.Description:
A use-after-free vulnerability exists in libcurl when an application
configures an HTTP/2 stream-dependency tree via `CURLOPT_STREAM_DEPENDS` or
`CURLOPT_STREAM_DEPENDS_E`, subsequently invokes `curl_easy_reset()`, and
finally terminates the handle with `curl_easy_cleanup()`. During this final
cleanup phase, libcurl attempts to access and modify an internal structure
that was already freed during the reset operation.

Vulnerabilities.Title: curl: curl: Information disclosure via incorrect Digest authentication header reuse
Vulnerabilities.Description:
Successfully using libcurl to do a transfer to a specific HTTP origin
(`hostA`) with **Digest** authentication and then changing the origin to a
different one (`hostB`) for a second transfer, reusing the same handle, makes
libcurl wrongly pass on the `Authorization:` header field meant for `hostA`,
to `hostB`.

Vulnerabilities.Title: curl: libcurl: Information disclosure via incorrect connection reuse with Negotiate authentication
Vulnerabilities.Description:
A flaw in libcurl makes it wrongly reuse an HTTP connection setup for a given
hostname using Negotiate authentication, when the initial request is done
using empty credentials. This can make user B's request get sent over user A's
previously authenticated connection.

Vulnerabilities.Title: curl: curl: Information disclosure via incorrect .netrc password lookup
Vulnerabilities.Description:
When asking curl to use a `.netrc` file to find credentials and at the same
time specifying a URL with a username (without a password), like
`https://user@example.com/`, curl could wrongly get and use the password for
*another* user set in the `.netrc` file for that host if such a one exists and
there is no match for the specified user.

Vulnerabilities.Title: libcurl: libcurl: Security feature bypass due to improper mTLS connection reuse
Vulnerabilities.Description:
libcurl would reuse a previously created connection even when some mTLS config
related option had been changed that should have prohibited reuse.

libcurl keeps previously used connections in a connection pool for subsequent
transfers to reuse if one of them matches the setup. However, some TLS
settings related to client certificates were left out from the configuration
match checks, making them match too easily. In particular options related to
the private key.

Vulnerabilities.Title: libcurl: libcurl: Information disclosure due to failure to clear proxy authentication credentials
Vulnerabilities.Description:
libcurl had a flaw that when instructed to clear proxy authentication
credentials which made it not do so, leaving the old credentials around to get
used for subsequent transfers that should not know nor use them.

Vulnerabilities.Title: libcurl: libcurl: Use-after-free via curl_easy_pause() in CURLMOPT_SOCKETFUNCTION callback
Vulnerabilities.Description:
Calling `curl_easy_pause()` within the event-based `CURLMOPT_SOCKETFUNCTION`
callback triggers a use-after-free vulnerability, where libcurl attempts to
store a flag using a dangling struct pointer immediately after that pointer's
memory has been freed.

Vulnerabilities.Title: curl: curl: FTP wildcard write callback mixup
Vulnerabilities.Description:
When an FTP wildcard `LIST` operation fails, libcurl omits the restoration
path meant for successful listings, leaving the write callback set to the
internal listing parser and the write callback data pointing directly to the
easy handle. Subsequent reuse of this handle triggers an immediate crash, and
cloning it via `curl_easy_duphandle()` copies this corrupted state into the
duplicate. If the original handle is subsequently freed, executing a transfer
on the cloned handle causes a heap use-after-free read against the dangling
handle reference; alternatively, reusing the original or cloned handle while
changing only  `CURLOPT_WRITEDATA` (and omitting `CURLOPT_WRITEFUNCTION`)
results in type confusion, forcing the internal parser to interpret incoming
server response bytes into memory at the application-supplied write data
pointer.

Vulnerabilities.Title: libcurl: libcurl: Information disclosure via cached SSL session and early data
Vulnerabilities.Description:
In this scenario, libcurl first uses a proper HTTP/3 server for the initial
transfers, and when it makes a second transfer to the same site it has been
replaced by the attacker's impostor machine - without a valid certificate.

When libcurl returns to the hostname the second time with a cached SSL session
(`CURLOPT_SSL_SESSIONID_CACHE` is not disabled) and early data enabled (the
`CURLSSLOPT_EARLYDATA` bit is set in `CURLOPT_SSL_OPTIONS`), libcurl might
send off the second request's bytes on that new connection *before* enforcing
the certificate verification failure. Potentially leaking sensitive
information.

Vulnerabilities.Title: curl: Curl missing SFTP host verification with wolfSSH backend
Vulnerabilities.Description:
curl's code for managing SSH connections when SFTP was done using the wolfSSH
powered backend was flawed and missed host verification mechanisms.

This prevents curl from detecting MITM attackers and more.

Vulnerabilities.Title: curl: curl: Security bypass due to global TLS option changes in multi-threaded LDAPS transfers
Vulnerabilities.Description:
When doing multi-threaded LDAPS transfers (LDAP over TLS) with libcurl,
changing TLS options in one thread would inadvertently change them globally
and therefore possibly also affect other concurrently setup transfers.

Disabling certificate verification for a specific transfer could
unintentionally disable the feature for other threads as well.

Vulnerabilities.Title: curl: Host verification bypass during SSH transfers
Vulnerabilities.Description:
When doing SSH-based transfers using either SCP or SFTP, and setting the
known_hosts file, libcurl could still mistakenly accept connecting to hosts
*not present* in the specified file if they were added as recognized in the
libssh *global* known_hosts file.

Vulnerabilities.Title: curl: libssh key passphrase bypass without agent set
Vulnerabilities.Description:
When doing SSH-based transfers using either SCP or SFTP, and asked to do
public key authentication, curl would wrongly still ask and authenticate using
a locally running SSH agent.

Vulnerabilities.Title: curl: curl: info leak uploading over WebSockets with GnuTLS
Vulnerabilities.Description:
When curl is built with GnuTLS, a malicious WebSocket server can make curl
send memory past its send buffer. This is due to an out of bounds read
following when `gnutls_record_send()` returns a number of bytes sent **greater
than the number of bytes it was given to send**. GnuTLS does that after a
blocked send.

Vulnerabilities.Title: curl: curl: local interface connection reuse mixup
Vulnerabilities.Description:
When `CURLOPT_INTERFACE` (or the command line tool's `--interface` option) is
set with one of the documented prefixes (`if!`, `host!`, `ifhost!`), that
binding is not part of the connection reuse key, so a later transfer asking
for a different source can silently reuse an existing connection and go out
from the earlier transfer's source address

Vulnerabilities.Title: curl: curl: Authentication bypass in OpenLDAP SASL negotiation via Man-in-the-Middle (MITM) attack
Vulnerabilities.Description:
A flaw in the libcurl SASL negotiation for LDAP authentication allows an
incomplete handshake sequence to be misinterpreted as a successful
cryptographic verification. An attacker executing a Man-in-the-Middle (MITM)
attack can inject a premature or shortcut response that bypasses complete peer
validation.

Vulnerabilities.Title: curl: libcurl: Use-after-free in HTTP/2 Server Push with shared connections
Vulnerabilities.Description:
A flaw in libcurl's handling of HTTP/2 Server Push streams, when the parent
handle is set to share connections with other handles, can lead to
use-after-free in the cleanup process.

Vulnerabilities.Title: curl: libcurl: Memory corruption vulnerability via OpenSSL 3 provider use-after-free
Vulnerabilities.Description:
When performing transfers via libcurl’s multi interface, pooled TLS
connections can outlive their originating easy handles. In OpenSSL 3 provider
configurations, libcurl attaches an allocated library context to the easy
handle's state and passes it to OpenSSL without acquiring an ownership
reference; destroying the easy handle prematurely frees this context while the
active connection retains a dangling pointer, leading to a heap-use-after-free
upon subsequent I/O or post-handshake operations.

Vulnerabilities.Title: curl: curl: Public key pinning bypass allows unauthenticated connections
Vulnerabilities.Description:
When `CURLOPT_PINNEDPUBLICKEY` is configured alongside options that disable
standard peer verification (`CURLOPT_SSL_VERIFYPEER = 0` and
`CURLOPT_SSL_VERIFYHOST = 0`), libcurl fails to enforce public key pinning on
connections established without a presented server certificate. Bypassing the
pinning check under these disabled-verification conditions allows
unauthenticated connections to succeed when they should be rejected.

Vulnerabilities.Title: curl: curl: Information disclosure due to secure cookie attribute bypass
Vulnerabilities.Description:
A `Set-Cookie:` header using tab (horizontal tab, ASCII code 9) instead of
space (ascii code 32) immediately before the `Secure` attribute causes curl to
store the cookie without its Secure flag. The cookie might then wrongfully be
sent over plaintext HTTP on subsequent requests to the same host.

Vulnerabilities.Title: curl: libcurl: Improper certificate validation when using wolfSSL CA cache
Vulnerabilities.Description:
With the wolfSSL backend, when CA caching is enabled and an
`CURLOPT_SSL_CTX_FUNCTION` callback replaces the trust store, libcurl can
silently reinstall the cached store after the callback returns. A certificate
trusted by the cached store but rejected by the callback-selected store is
then incorrectly accepted.

Vulnerabilities.Title: curl: libcurl: Information disclosure via improper Public Suffix List boundary check
Vulnerabilities.Description:
When libpsl support is enabled, libcurl fails to enforce the Public Suffix
List boundary check when processing a `Set-Cookie` header where the `Domain`
attribute explicitly matches an origin host that is itself a public suffix
(e.g., `Domain=co.uk` set by `co.uk`).

Instead of coercing it into a strict host-only cookie, libcurl saves the
cookie with wildcard domain scope (`.co.uk`). Consequently, the cookie is
inappropriately included in subsequent outbound requests or HTTP redirects to
arbitrary sibling subdomains under the same public suffix (e.g.,
`attacker.co.uk`).

Vulnerabilities.Title: curl: curl: stale SigV4 headers sent unintended
Vulnerabilities.Description:
Setting `CURLOPT_AWS_SIGV4` to NULL but does not disable SigV4 authentication,
contrary to expectations and documentation. A subsequent transfer on the same
handle still sends an `Authorization: AWS4-HMAC-SHA256` header to whatever URL
isset next, leaking state information.

Vulnerabilities.Title: curl: curl: redirect to SFTP or SCP bypasses host verification
Vulnerabilities.Description:
A flaw in the curl command line tool's logic makes it only set SSH host
verification options when interacting directly using SFTP or SCP, and not as a
result of following a redirect.

Vulnerabilities.Title: curl: curl: leaking host credentials to HTTP proxy
Vulnerabilities.Description:
An HTTP proxy can trick libcurl into sending the origin's credentials (Basic
password, or a Negotiate/Kerberos ticket) to the proxy itself, by answering
the `CONNECT` tunnel request with 401 `WWW-Authenticate:` instead of the
expected 407 `Proxy-Authenticate:`.

Vulnerabilities.Title: curl: curl: HSTS cache import drops longer-lived child
Vulnerabilities.Description:
Importing a `includeSubDomains` parent HSTS entry before a longer-lived child
entry, silently drops the child. Consequently, when the parent expires, the
child's valid HSTS policy is lost, causing curl to issue unencrypted HTTP
requests rather than upgrading to HTTPS.

Vulnerabilities.Title: curl: curl: Hsts Response Erases Persisted Entries
Vulnerabilities.Description:
An authenticated HTTPS origin can supply an HSTS `max-age` value that the
parser accepts, but time serialization later fails to process. On 64-bit
systems, extreme max-age values compute an absolute expiry within standard
time integer limits that exceeds calendar time structure bounds. During cache
saves, the original HSTS file is truncated before writing a temporary
replacement; when serialization fails, the temporary file is deleted, leaving
an empty or partial cache. Because the save error is silently ignored during
cleanup, curl exits successfully despite the data loss.

Vulnerabilities.Title: curl: IMAP APPEND plus CRLF conversion command injection
Vulnerabilities.Description:
Enabling `CURLOPT_CRLF` causes curl to advertise the raw input byte count in
the `IMAP APPEND {N}` literal while transmitting line-ending expanded data.
The server reads only $N$ bytes for the payload, causing the remaining
overflow bytes to be interpreted and executed as pipelined IMAP commands
within the authenticated session.

Vulnerabilities.Title: curl: curl: knownhost callback mismatches key as missing
Vulnerabilities.Description:
When libcurl uses libssh2 with a hashed `known_hosts` file, an unrelated
initial entry can cause host key validation to report a key *mismatch* as a
*missing* key to the `CURLOPT_SSH_KEYFUNCTION` callback.

Vulnerabilities.Title: curl: curl: wolfSSL public-key pinning bypass
Vulnerabilities.Description:
When built with wolfSSL, curl can successfully validate a pinned public key
hash against a key the TLS peer does not possess. During the TLS handshake,
wolfSSL validates the connection, but curl's subsequent re-parsing of the same
certificate - tricked by a manipulated validity length field - extracts and
matches a different embedded key, incorrectly authorizing the pinned public
key.

Vulnerabilities.Title: curl: curl: server-set cookie aborts cookie jar load
Vulnerabilities.Description:
When writing a long cookie name and value to a Netscape cookie jar, a remote
HTTP server can make `curl` write a record that exceeds its line-length
parsing limit. Consequently, any subsequent `curl` invocation reading from
that same cookie jar using `--cookie` silently aborts parsing prematurely upon
encountering the too long line, ignoring all subsequent valid cookies in the
file.

Vulnerabilities.Title: curl: curl: never-ending loop via server response omission
Vulnerabilities.Description:
By permanently omitting the final control-response line, a malicious FTP,
IMAP, POP3, or SMTP server can exploit libcurl and completely bypass its
configured transfer timeout mechanism, indefinitely blocking all concurrent
transfers bound to the same multi-handle.

Vulnerabilities.Title: curl: curl: TFTP direction confusion
Vulnerabilities.Description:
libcurl's TFTP state machine fails to validate state transitions against the
requested transfer direction, accepting opening server responses for both
reads and writes interchangeably. A malicious TFTP server can respond to a
download request in a way that forces the client into transmit mode, prompting
libcurl to consume and transmit data from the handle's persistent
`CURLOPT_READDATA` pointer - including data remaining from unrelated prior
operations, such as an HTTP POST request executed on a reused handle.

Vulnerabilities.Title: curl: curl: -J no-clobber guarantee bypassed with 103 early hints
Vulnerabilities.Description:
When invoked with `--remote-header-name` (`-J`), curl fails to preserve its
documented anti-clobbering protection if an intermediate 103 Early Hints
response precedes the final HTTP response, or if an `ETag` header is processed
before `Content-Disposition` under `--etag-save`. This flaw allows an HTTP(S)
server to overwrite an existing local file specified in the
`Content-Disposition` header despite the presence of the `-J` non-overwrite
constraint.

Vulnerabilities.Title: curl: curl: curl_mime_free stack overflow by recursion
Vulnerabilities.Description:
A deeply nested multipart MIME structure constructed via the public API causes
a stack overflow in libcurl during normal cleanup operations. An excessive
recursion depth within `curl_mime_free` leads to unbounded stack frame
allocation during structure traversal, ultimately crashing the host process.

Vulnerabilities.Title: curl: curl: password leak in CURLINFO_EFFECTIVE_URL
Vulnerabilities.Description:
libcurl could accidentally return a URL for `curl_easy_getinfo()`'s
`CURLINFO_EFFECTIVE_URL` option containing credentials, even though neither
the URL provided to libcurl nor the redirected URL did.

Vulnerabilities.Title: curl: curl: Man-in-the-middle attack via SSH host key bypass
Vulnerabilities.Description:
When a libcurl-based application performs transfers via `SCP://` or `SFTP://`
and utilizes the `CURLOPT_SSH_KEYFUNCTION` callback, it may silently accept an
untrusted server. This vulnerability occurs when a server presents a host key
type that does not match the specific key type already recorded for that host
in the `known_hosts` file. Instead of rejecting the mismatch, the callback
mechanism fails to properly enforce the restriction, allowing the connection
to succeed without warning and risking a potential man-in-the-middle attack.

Vulnerabilities.Title: dash: dash: Super-polynomial backtracking in pmatch when libc fnmatch is disabled
Vulnerabilities.Description: A flaw was found in dash. When built without libc fnmatch, the internal pmatch() matcher implements * by unbounded recursion over candidate positions. A local user who can plant filenames, or otherwise feed that matcher, can make a short multi-star pattern such as *.*.*.*.*.tar.gz consume excessive CPU.

Vulnerabilities.Title: dash: dash: Heap out-of-bounds write in conv_escape via undersized Unicode escape reservation
Vulnerabilities.Description: A flaw was found in dash. The printf builtin reserves four bytes before converting a Unicode \u or \U escape, but the multi-byte token can need five or six bytes. A local user who can supply such an escape to dash printf or echo %b, including through dash -c and a positional argument, can write one or two bytes past that reservation.

Vulnerabilities.Title: diffutils: heap‑based buffer overflow due to multiple signed integer overflows in line‑mapping calculations
Vulnerabilities.Description:
diff3 tool from GNU diffutils is vulnerable to a heap‑based buffer overflow due to multiple signed integer overflows in line‑mapping calculations. Incorrect arithmetic in mapping line ranges can result in corrupted values being used for memory allocation and loop bounds.
When processing crafted diff output, these overflows may cause the application to allocate insufficient memory and subsequently perform out‑of‑bounds writes during internal processing. 
An attacker who can control the output of the diff program used by diff3 (e.g. via --diff-program pointing to a malicious script) can trigger out-of-bounds writes, resulting in a crash and potentially remote code execution depending on the environment.


This issue has been fixed in commit 9ff04d5b84743e331e80b589335a52c5480d1815 

NOTE:
The project maintainers claim that this is not a security issue. They state that the worst outcome this issue can cause is a crash of diff and that it cannot be used to escalate privileges.

Vulnerabilities.Title: GnuPG: GnuPG: Stack-based buffer overflow in tpm2daemon allows arbitrary code execution
Vulnerabilities.Description: In GnuPG before 2.5.17, a stack-based buffer overflow exists in tpm2daemon during handling of the PKDECRYPT command for TPM-backed RSA and ECC keys.

Vulnerabilities.Title: gnupg: GnuPG: Signature bypass via form feed character in signed messages
Vulnerabilities.Description: In GnuPG through 2.4.8, if a signed message has \f at the end of a plaintext line, an adversary can construct a modified message that places additional text after the signed material, such that signature verification of the modified message succeeds (although an "invalid armor" message is printed during verification). This is related to use of \f as a marker to denote truncation of a long plaintext line.

Vulnerabilities.Title: gnupg: denial of service issue (resource consumption) using compressed packets
Vulnerabilities.Description: GnuPG can be made to spin on a relatively small input by (for example) crafting a public key with thousands of signatures attached, compressed down to just a few KB.

Vulnerabilities.Title: gnupg2: gnupg: Arbitrary file overwrite via symlink traversal in gpgtar
Vulnerabilities.Description: gpgtar in GnuPG before 2.5.19 can allow file overwrite via crafted data in an archive. When extracting an untrusted archive with --directory (aka -C) into an existing directory containing a pre-existing symlink, gpgtar can follow that symlink and create or overwrite a file outside the selected extraction directory. The write is limited by the extraction user's filesystem permissions. An archive extracted into a fresh empty directory does not have this risk.

Vulnerabilities.Title: GnuPG: Incorrect cryptographic message parsing
Vulnerabilities.Description: CMS (Cryptographic Message Syntax) parsing in gpgsm in GnuPG through 2.5.20 mishandles the CMS format for AES-GCM because aes-ICVlen is supposed to be 12 bytes but 4 bytes is accepted. NOTE: this is related to CVE-2026-34182.

Vulnerabilities.Title: A directory traversal bug was discovered when unpacking 3.0 (quilt) so ...
Vulnerabilities.Description: A directory traversal bug was discovered when unpacking 3.0 (quilt) source packages, where the packaging tarball could contain the quilt database directory (.pc) with attacker controlled symlinks, where that in combination with patches that would fail to apply, could be used to make the code used to restore the backup files to either modify or remove the files pointed to by the attacker controlled symlinks.

Vulnerabilities.Title: gcc-toolset-15-gcc: gcc: gcc-toolset-16: gcc: Denial of Service via use-after-free in binary heap erase_if
Vulnerabilities.Description: A flaw was found in GCC. When an application calls the erase_if function on a binary heap priority queue in libstdc++, the library reallocates storage but fails to update its internal entry pointer. An attacker capable of triggering this operation can exploit this use-after-free condition, leading to a Denial of Service (DoS) via an application crash or potential memory corruption.

Vulnerabilities.Title: gcc: Confirmed out-of-bounds read/write in libstdc++ parallel `std
Vulnerabilities.Description: A flaw was found in GCC. An out-of-bounds memory access vulnerability exists in the libstdc++ parallel search implementation due to an undersized internal buffer. A local attacker can exploit this flaw by providing crafted search data to an application compiled with parallel mode, causing the process to crash and leading to a Denial of Service (DoS).

Vulnerabilities.Title: gcc: Integer wrap in `std
Vulnerabilities.Description: A flaw was found in the libstdc++ component of GCC. An attacker who can provide an excessively large element count to a boolean vector (std::vector<bool>) constructor can trigger an integer wrap during internal memory calculations. This issue leaves the container in an inconsistent state, leading to out-of-bounds memory access and resulting in an application crash or a Denial of Service (DoS) during subsequent operations.

Vulnerabilities.Title: gcc: Stack overflow in std::bitset on libstdc++
Vulnerabilities.Description: A flaw was found in GCC libstdc++. When an application extracts data into a bitset from a wide-character stream, internal stack memory allocation fails to properly account for character size and alignment. An attacker capable of supplying crafted input to an affected application could trigger a stack-based buffer overflow leading denial of service (DoS).

Vulnerabilities.Title: libstdc++: overflow leaves streambuf in inconsistent state on I/O error.
Vulnerabilities.Description: A flaw was found in libstdc++. When a byte-by-byte write operation fails during file stream processing, the library may still append data into the internal memory buffer. An attacker capable of inducing repeated write failures in an affected service can trigger a buffer overflow, potentially resulting in a Denial of Service (DoS) or memory corruption.

Vulnerabilities.Title: gcc: libstdc++ integer overflow in `new` operator
Vulnerabilities.Description: A flaw was found in libstdc++. An integer overflow can occur when processing large inputs to the aligned operator new in the C++ library. This vulnerability could lead to an undersized memory allocation, potentially causing memory corruption or application instability.

Vulnerabilities.Title: gcc: Out-of-bounds read in std::from_chars
Vulnerabilities.Description: A flaw was found in gcc. An attacker could cause a Denial of Service (DoS) by passing a string that is not null-terminated to the std::from_chars() function in the libstdc++ library. This issue triggers an out-of-bounds read beyond the allocated buffer, potentially leading to invalid data parsing or an application crash.

Vulnerabilities.Title: ghostscript: Heap buffer overflow in Ghostscript TrueType outliner due to nPointsTotal integer underflow during retry rollback
Vulnerabilities.Description: A flaw was found in Ghostscript. When processing a specially crafted TrueType font or document embedding one, an accounting error during font rendering can bypass buffer size checks, triggering a heap-based buffer overflow. A remote attacker could exploit this by enticing a victim or automated service to open the malicious content, potentially resulting in a Denial of Service (DoS) crash or arbitrary code execution.

Vulnerabilities.Title: Artifex Ghostscript: Artifex Ghostscript: Denial of Service via crafted document processing
Vulnerabilities.Description: In Artifex Ghostscript through 10.05.1, ocr_begin_page in devices/gdevpdfocr.c has an integer overflow that leads to a heap-based buffer overflow in ocr_line8.

Vulnerabilities.Title: In Artifex GhostXPS before 10.06.0, there is a stack-based buffer over ...
Vulnerabilities.Description: In Artifex GhostXPS before 10.06.0, there is a stack-based buffer overflow in xps_unpredict_tiff in xpstiff.c because the samplesperpixel value is not checked.

Vulnerabilities.Title: ghostscript: Out-of-bounds read in ghostscript shade_next_color via integer overflow of indexed color index in mesh shading
Vulnerabilities.Description: A flaw was found in Ghostscript. A remote attacker could exploit this vulnerability by enticing a user to process a specially crafted PDF or PostScript document containing malicious mesh shading data. Due to improper bounds validation during the processing of indexed color values, Ghostscript triggers an out-of-bounds memory read. Successful exploitation can lead to a Denial of Service (DoS) through an application crash or result in limited information disclosure.

Vulnerabilities.Title: GnuPG: GnuPG: Stack-based buffer overflow in tpm2daemon allows arbitrary code execution
Vulnerabilities.Description: In GnuPG before 2.5.17, a stack-based buffer overflow exists in tpm2daemon during handling of the PKDECRYPT command for TPM-backed RSA and ECC keys.

Vulnerabilities.Title: gnupg: GnuPG: Signature bypass via form feed character in signed messages
Vulnerabilities.Description: In GnuPG through 2.4.8, if a signed message has \f at the end of a plaintext line, an adversary can construct a modified message that places additional text after the signed material, such that signature verification of the modified message succeeds (although an "invalid armor" message is printed during verification). Vulnerabilities.Description: GnuPG can be made to spin on a relatively small input by (for example) crafting a public key with thousands of signatures attached, compressed down to just a few KB.

Vulnerabilities.Title: gnupg2: gnupg: Arbitrary file overwrite via symlink traversal in gpgtar
Vulnerabilities.Description: gpgtar in GnuPG before 2.5.19 can allow file overwrite via crafted data in an archive. When extracting an untrusted archive with --directory (aka -C) into an existing directory containing a pre-existing symlink, gpgtar can follow that symlink and create or overwrite a file outside the selected extraction directory. The write is limited by the extraction user's filesystem permissions. An archive extracted into a fresh empty directory does not have this risk.

Vulnerabilities.Description: CMS (Cryptographic Message Syntax) parsing in gpgsm in GnuPG through 2.5.20 mishandles the CMS format for AES-GCM because aes-ICVlen is supposed to be 12 bytes but 4 bytes is accepted. NOTE: this is related to CVE-2026-34182.

Vulnerabilities.Title: Artifex Software jbig2dec v0.20 was discovered to contain a SEGV vulne ...
Vulnerabilities.Description: Artifex Software jbig2dec v0.20 was discovered to contain a SEGV vulnerability via jbig2_error at /jbig2dec/jbig2.c.

Vulnerabilities.Title: acl: Symlink traversal privilege escalation via libacl functions
Vulnerabilities.Description: acl before version 2.4.0 contains a symlink traversal vulnerability in the libacl pathname-based functions acl_get_file(), acl_set_file(), acl_extended_file(), and acl_delete_def_file() that allows local attackers to escalate privileges by replacing any pathname component with a symbolic link. Attackers who control any component of a pathname processed by a privileged caller can redirect ACL read or write operations to arbitrary files or directories, enabling unauthorized manipulation of access control lists and local privilege escalation.

Vulnerabilities.Title: acl: TOCTOU Symlink Traversal via getfacl/setfacl
Vulnerabilities.Description: acl before version 2.4.0 contains a time-of-check to time-of-use (TOCTOU) race condition vulnerability that allows local attackers to escalate privileges by replacing a pathname component with a symbolic link between an lstat() check and subsequent symlink-following operations such as stat(), chown(), chmod(), acl_get_file(), and acl_set_file(). Attackers who control a pathname component can redirect file access control list operations to arbitrary files when getfacl, setfacl, or chacl is invoked by a privileged process over an attacker-controlled path, resulting in local privilege escalation.

Vulnerabilities.Title: apt: apt: Remote code execution via hard link reuse during package download retries
Vulnerabilities.Description:
On Debian, Ubuntu, and derivative Linux distributions, an on-path attacker who can manipulate the HTTP traffic (including a malicious mirror or proxy) between an APT client and an archive server triggered by a package install can trick the client into installing an attacker-controlled unverified package and achieve remote code execution with root privileges.



The vulnerability is caused by the reuse of hard links and requires the client to follow redirects and retry the download of package files. It requires the client to have a non-zero Acquire::Retries configuration setting; the value 3 is the default starting with Debian 12 (bookworm) and Ubuntu 22.04 LTS (Jammy Jellyfish), so older releases are unaffected in a default configuration

Vulnerabilities.Title: It was found that apt-key in apt, all versions, do not correctly valid ...
Vulnerabilities.Description: It was found that apt-key in apt, all versions, do not correctly validate gpg keys with the master keyring, leading to a potential man-in-the-middle attack.

Vulnerabilities.Title: libarchive: Double-Free Vulnerability in RAR5 Decompression Logic via dangling filtered_buf pointer in init_unpack()
Vulnerabilities.Description: A double free issue has been identified in libarchive's RAR5 reader. During parsing of a specially crafted RAR5 archive, the filtered_buf pointer may remain stale after being freed during unpacking state reinitialization. Subsequent processing of another archive entry can trigger a second free of the same memory region, resulting in a double-free condition. Successful exploitation may cause applications using the vulnerable libarchive API to terminate unexpectedly, leading to a denial of service.

Vulnerabilities.Title: libarchive: heap overflow OOB read while parsing a tar archive contains a PAX extended header
Vulnerabilities.Description: A flaw was found in libarchive. This vulnerability allows a remote attacker to trigger a heap overflow by providing a specially crafted tar archive. The issue occurs during the parsing of a PAX extended header containing a malformed SUN.holesdata sparse-file attribute. Successful exploitation could lead to a denial of service, making the system unavailable, or potentially allow for arbitrary code execution, giving the attacker control over the affected system.

Vulnerabilities.Title: libarchive: Race condition in multi-threaded use of archive_write_disk_header() on posix based systems
Vulnerabilities.Description: Libarchive through 3.6.2 can cause directories to have world-writable permissions. The umask() call inside archive_write_disk_posix.c changes the umask of the whole process for a very short period of time; a race condition with another thread can lead to a permanent umask 0 setting. Such a race condition could lead to implicit directory creation with permissions 0777 (without the sticky bit), which means that any low-privileged local user can delete and rename files inside those directories.

Vulnerabilities.Title: libarchive: Buffer Overflow vulnerability in libarchive
Vulnerabilities.Description: list_item_verbose in tar/util.c in libarchive through 3.7.7 does not check an strftime return value, which can lead to a denial of service or unspecified other impact via a crafted TAR archive that is read with a verbose value of 2. For example, the 100-byte buffer may not be sufficient for a custom locale.

Vulnerabilities.Title: libarchive: bsdtar hangs and OOMs with zero-length pattern matches
Vulnerabilities.Description: An issue was discovered in libarchive bsdtar before version 3.8.1 in function apply_substitution in file tar/subst.c when processing crafted -s substitution rules. This can cause unbounded memory allocation and lead to denial of service (Out-of-Memory crash).

Vulnerabilities.Title: libarchive: libarchive: Signed Integer Overflow in archive_write_zip_header
Vulnerabilities.Description: A signed integer overflow vulnerability was found in libarchive's ZIP writer. In the archive_write_zip_header function in archive_write_set_format_zip.c, when ZIP encryption is enabled and the entry file size is close to INT64_MAX, the addition of the encryption overhead to the entry size overflows int64_t, resulting in undefined behavior. This could lead to incorrect Zip64 extension decisions or potential memory corruption.

Vulnerabilities.Title: libarchive: libarchive: use-after-free via aliased Mac metadata copy
Vulnerabilities.Description: A flaw was found in libarchive. An attacker can cause a Denial of Service (DoS) or potential information disclosure due to a use-after-free vulnerability, which occurs when a program reads memory that has already been released. This issue arises when the archive_entry_copy_mac_metadata() function deallocates an internal buffer before completing a data copy. An attacker who can supply input to an application utilizing this function can trigger the flaw to crash the application or read uninitialized memory data.

Vulnerabilities.Title: libarchive: A NULL pointer dereference vulnerability exists in the ACL parser of libarchive
Vulnerabilities.Description: A flaw was found in libarchive. A NULL pointer dereference vulnerability exists in the ACL parsing logic, specifically within the archive_acl_from_text_nl() function. When processing a malformed ACL string (such as a bare "d" or "default" tag without subsequent fields), the function fails to perform adequate validation before advancing the pointer. An attacker can exploit this by providing a maliciously crafted archive, causing an application utilizing the libarchive API (such as bsdtar) to crash, resulting in a Denial of Service (DoS).

Vulnerabilities.Title: gcc-toolset-15-gcc: gcc: gcc-toolset-16: gcc: Denial of Service via use-after-free in binary heap erase_if
Vulnerabilities.Description: A flaw was found in GCC. When an application calls the erase_if function on a binary heap priority queue in libstdc++, the library reallocates storage but fails to update its internal entry pointer. An attacker capable of triggering this operation can exploit this use-after-free condition, leading to a Denial of Service (DoS) via an application crash or potential memory corruption.

Vulnerabilities.Title: gcc: Confirmed out-of-bounds read/write in libstdc++ parallel `std
Vulnerabilities.Description: A flaw was found in GCC. An out-of-bounds memory access vulnerability exists in the libstdc++ parallel search implementation due to an undersized internal buffer. A local attacker can exploit this flaw by providing crafted search data to an application compiled with parallel mode, causing the process to crash and leading to a Denial of Service (DoS).

Vulnerabilities.Title: gcc: Integer wrap in `std
Vulnerabilities.Description: A flaw was found in the libstdc++ component of GCC. An attacker who can provide an excessively large element count to a boolean vector (std::vector<bool>) constructor can trigger an integer wrap during internal memory calculations. This issue leaves the container in an inconsistent state, leading to out-of-bounds memory access and resulting in an application crash or a Denial of Service (DoS) during subsequent operations.

Vulnerabilities.Title: gcc: Stack overflow in std::bitset on libstdc++
Vulnerabilities.Description: A flaw was found in GCC libstdc++. When an application extracts data into a bitset from a wide-character stream, internal stack memory allocation fails to properly account for character size and alignment. An attacker capable of supplying crafted input to an affected application could trigger a stack-based buffer overflow leading denial of service (DoS).

Vulnerabilities.Title: libstdc++: overflow leaves streambuf in inconsistent state on I/O error.
Vulnerabilities.Description: A flaw was found in libstdc++. When a byte-by-byte write operation fails during file stream processing, the library may still append data into the internal memory buffer. An attacker capable of inducing repeated write failures in an affected service can trigger a buffer overflow, potentially resulting in a Denial of Service (DoS) or memory corruption.

Vulnerabilities.Title: gcc: libstdc++ integer overflow in `new` operator
Vulnerabilities.Description: A flaw was found in libstdc++. An integer overflow can occur when processing large inputs to the aligned operator new in the C++ library. This vulnerability could lead to an undersized memory allocation, potentially causing memory corruption or application instability.

Vulnerabilities.Title: gcc: Out-of-bounds read in std::from_chars
Vulnerabilities.Description: A flaw was found in gcc. An attacker could cause a Denial of Service (DoS) by passing a string that is not null-terminated to the std::from_chars() function in the libstdc++ library. This issue triggers an out-of-bounds read beyond the allocated buffer, potentially leading to invalid data parsing or an application crash.

Vulnerabilities.Title: attr: attr: Symlink Traversal Privilege Escalation via getfattr and setfattr
Vulnerabilities.Description: attr before version 2.6.0 contains a symlink traversal vulnerability in the getfattr and setfattr utilities that allows local attackers to escalate privileges by replacing a pathname component with a symbolic link during directory hierarchy traversal. Attackers who control a pathname component can redirect getfattr and setfattr operations to arbitrary files by substituting a symlink, leading to local privilege escalation when getfattr or setfattr is invoked by a privileged process over an attacker-controlled path.

Vulnerabilities.Title: avahi: Avahi Wide-Area DNS Uses Constant Source Port
Vulnerabilities.Description: A flaw was found in Avahi-daemon, which relies on fixed source ports for wide-area DNS queries. This issue simplifies attacks where malicious DNS responses are injected.

Vulnerabilities.Title: avahi: Avahi Wide-Area DNS Predictable Transaction IDs
Vulnerabilities.Description: A flaw was found in the Avahi-daemon, where it initializes DNS transaction IDs randomly only once at startup, incrementing them sequentially after that. This predictable behavior facilitates DNS spoofing attacks, allowing attackers to guess transaction IDs.

Vulnerabilities.Title: avahi: simple clients denial-of-service
Vulnerabilities.Description: Avahi is a system which facilitates service discovery on a local network via the mDNS/DNS-SD protocol suite. In versions up to and including 0.9-rc5, the simple protocol server ignores the documented client limit and accepts unlimited connections, allowing for easy local DoS. Although `CLIENTS_MAX` is defined, `server_work()` unconditionally `accept()`s and `client_new()` always appends the new client and increments `n_clients`. There is no check against the limit. When client cannot be accepted as a result of maximal socket number of avahi-daemon, it logs unconditionally error per each connection. Unprivileged local users can exhaust daemon memory and file descriptors, causing a denial of service system-wide for mDNS/DNS-SD. Exhausting local file descriptors causes increased system load caused by logging errors of each of request. Overloading prevents glibc calls using nss-mdns plugins to resolve `*.local.` names and link-local addresses. As of time of publication, no known patched versions are available, but a candidate fix is available in pull request 808, and some workarounds are available. Simple clients are offered for nss-mdns package functionality. It is not possible to disable the unix socket `/run/avahi-daemon/socket`, but resolution requests received via DBus are not affected directly. Tools avahi-resolve, avahi-resolve-address and avahi-resolve-host-name are not affected, they use DBus interface. It is possible to change permissions of unix socket after avahi-daemon is started. But avahi-daemon does not provide any configuration for it. Additional access restrictions like SELinux can also prevent unwanted tools to access the socket and keep resolution working for trusted users.

Vulnerabilities.Title: avahi: Avahi: Denial of Service via D-Bus record browsers with AVAHI_LOOKUP_USE_WIDE_AREA flag
Vulnerabilities.Description:
Avahi is a system which facilitates service discovery on a local network via the mDNS/DNS-SD protocol suite. In 0.9-rc2 and earlier, an unprivileged local users can crash avahi-daemon (with wide-area disabled) by creating record browsers with the AVAHI_LOOKUP_USE_WIDE_AREA flag set via D-Bus. This can be done by either calling
the RecordBrowserNew method directly or creating hostname/address/service resolvers/browsers that create those browsers internally themselves.

Vulnerabilities.Title: avahi: Avahi: Denial of Service via crafted mDNS/DNS-SD announcements
Vulnerabilities.Description: Avahi is a system which facilitates service discovery on a local network via the mDNS/DNS-SD protocol suite. In 0.9-rc2 and earlier, avahi-daemon can be crashed by sending unsolicited announcements containing CNAME resource records pointing it to resource records with short TTLs. As soon as they expire avahi-daemon crashes.

Vulnerabilities.Title: avahi: Avahi: Denial of Service via unsolicited CNAME announcements
Vulnerabilities.Description: Avahi is a system which facilitates service discovery on a local network via the mDNS/DNS-SD protocol suite. In 0.9-rc2 and earlier, avahi-daemon can be crashed by sending 2 unsolicited announcements with CNAME resource records 2 seconds apart.

Vulnerabilities.Title: avahi: Avahi: Denial of Service via recursive CNAME record in mDNS response
Vulnerabilities.Description: Avahi is a system which facilitates service discovery on a local network via the mDNS/DNS-SD protocol suite. In versions 0.9rc2 and below, avahi-daemon can be crashed via a segmentation fault by sending an unsolicited mDNS response containing a recursive CNAME record, where the alias and canonical name point to the same domain (e.g., "h.local" as a CNAME for "h.local"). This causes unbounded recursion in the lookup_handle_cname function, leading to stack exhaustion. The vulnerability affects record browsers where AVAHI_LOOKUP_USE_MULTICAST is set explicitly, which includes record browsers created by resolvers used by nss-mdns. This issue is patched in commit 78eab31128479f06e30beb8c1cbf99dd921e2524, which is part of version 0.9-rc3.

Vulnerabilities.Title: avahi: avahi-daemon: Avahi: Denial of Service via D-Bus method call
Vulnerabilities.Description: Avahi is a system which facilitates service discovery on a local network via the mDNS/DNS-SD protocol suite. Prior to version 0.9-rc4, any unprivileged local user can crash avahi-daemon by sending a single D-Bus method call with conflicting publish flags. This issue has been patched in version 0.9-rc4.

Vulnerabilities.Title: avahi: Avahi: Denial of Service via crafted domain name over D-Bus
Vulnerabilities.Description: Avahi is a system which facilitates service discovery on a local network via the mDNS/DNS-SD protocol suite. In 0.9-rc4 and earlier, org.freedesktop.Avahi.Server.RecordBrowserNew accepts a domain-name value that avahi_is_valid_domain_name considers valid even though avahi_normalize_name_strdup cannot normalize it. The resulting null key reaches the key assertion in dbus_prepare_record_browser_object. A local low-privileged D-Bus client can trigger the mismatch and terminate the Avahi daemon, causing denial of service. The issue is fixed in 0.9-rc5.

Vulnerabilities.Description: A flaw was found in the Avahi-daemon, where it initializes DNS transaction IDs randomly only once at startup, incrementing them sequentially after that. This predictable behavior facilitates DNS spoofing attacks, allowing attackers to guess transaction IDs.

Vulnerabilities.Title: ffmpeg: heap buffer overflow in libwebp encoder conditional replenishment
Vulnerabilities.Description: FFmpeg through 9.0.2 contains a heap buffer overflow in ff_libwebp_get_frame() in libwebpenc_common.c that lets attackers corrupt memory when cr_threshold is set. Attackers can supply crafted media that increases resolution mid-stream, causing memcpy() to write pixel data past the stale reference frame and crash applications.

Vulnerabilities.Title: ffmpeg: heap buffer overflow via DVD subtitle encoder
Vulnerabilities.Description: FFmpeg before 8.1.3 and 9.x before 9.0.2 contains a heap buffer overflow vulnerability in the DVD subtitle encoder that underestimates RLE output size for odd-width rectangles. Attackers can supply files with crafted bitmap subtitles that, when transcoded to the dvdsub encoder, write past the output buffer and corrupt heap memory.

Vulnerabilities.Title: ffmpeg: out-of-bounds memory access in Huffyuv/FFVHUFF median predictor
Vulnerabilities.Description: FFmpeg through 9.0.2 contains an out-of-bounds memory access vulnerability in the encode_frame() function of libavcodec/huffyuvenc.c, because encode_init() never validates minimum frame dimensions for the median predictor. Attackers can supply a tiny video, such as a 2-pixel-wide or 1-2-pixel-tall frame, that causes negative sub_median_pred lengths and out-of-bounds reads and writes when transcoded to huffyuv or ffvhuff, crashing the encoder.

Vulnerabilities.Title: ffmpeg: heap buffer overflow via DVB subtitle encoder
Vulnerabilities.Description: FFmpeg through 9.0.2 contains a heap buffer overflow vulnerability in dvbsub_encode() in libavcodec/dvbsubenc.c that undercounts each CLUT segment header by two bytes. Attackers can supply a file with many bitmap subtitle rectangles that, when transcoded to the dvbsub encoder, writes past the output buffer and corrupts heap memory.

Vulnerabilities.Title: ffmpeg: VVC decoder out-of-bounds write via sh_entry_points()
Vulnerabilities.Description: FFmpeg before 8.1.3 and 9.x before 9.0.2 contains an out-of-bounds write vulnerability in the VVC decoder's sh_entry_points() function in libavcodec/vvc/ps.c. Attackers can supply a crafted VVC (H.266) bitstream whose SPS/PPS tile and WPP layout produces excess entry points, overflowing entry_point_start_ctu and corrupting decoder memory.

Vulnerabilities.Title: ffmpeg: heap buffer overflow via GIF encoder
Vulnerabilities.Description: FFmpeg through 9.0.2 contains a heap buffer overflow in the GIF encoder's gif_image_write_image() in libavcodec/gif.c because shrunk_buf is sized from the first frame's linesize. Attackers can supply PAL8 video whose frame linesize grows mid-stream, causing remap_frame_to_palette() to write past shrunk_buf and corrupt the heap during GIF transcoding.

Vulnerabilities.Title: ffmpeg: heap buffer overflow via LCEVC enhancement decoding
Vulnerabilities.Description: FFmpeg through 9.0.2 contains a heap buffer overflow vulnerability in libavcodec/lcevcdec.c because LCEVC output picture dimensions are not validated against the allocated frame. Attackers can embed crafted LCEVC enhancement data with differing global configurations in H.264 or HEVC streams to corrupt heap memory in decoding applications.

Vulnerabilities.Title: FFmpeg: FFmpeg: Memory corruption via crafted RASC video stream
Vulnerabilities.Description: FFmpeg's RASC video decoder (decode_dlta in libavcodec/rasc.c) performs 32-bit reads and writes at the row cursor before the NEXT_LINE row-boundary check and validates the DLTA region in pixel rather than byte units, so a DLTA run on a PAL8 frame can access several bytes past the row allocation. A crafted media stream using the RASC FourCC, decoded by libavcodec, triggers a bitstream-controlled out-of-bounds heap write and adjacent out-of-bounds read, leading to memory corruption.

Vulnerabilities.Title: ffmpeg: FFmpeg: Arbitrary code execution via heap buffer overflow in VobSub subtitle demuxer.
Vulnerabilities.Description: FFmpeg versions 2.1 through 8.1.2 contains a heap buffer overflow vulnerability in the VobSub subtitle demuxer that allows attackers to corrupt adjacent heap memory by supplying a malicious .sub/.idx subtitle file declaring more distinct stream IDs than the fixed-size array bounds in libavformat/mpeg.c. Attackers can craft a subtitle file with excessive distinct stream IDs to trigger unbounded writes beyond the vobsub->q[] array boundary via ff_subtitles_queue_insert(), potentially achieving arbitrary code execution in any application using FFmpeg's VobSub demuxer.

Vulnerabilities.Title: ffmpeg: FFmpeg: Arbitrary code execution via crafted video file in NVDEC hardware decoder
Vulnerabilities.Description: FFmpeg versions 4.4 through 8.1.2 contain a double-free vulnerability in the NVIDIA NVDEC hardware decoder within libavcodec/nvdec.c that allows attackers to trigger memory corruption by supplying a crafted video file. When no decoder surfaces remain, the ff_nvdec_start_frame_sep_ref error path frees memory via nvdec_fdd_priv_free while the calling layer subsequently frees the same frame description data, resulting in a double-free of the underlying decoder context in any FFmpeg-based application using NVDEC hardware-accelerated decoding.

Vulnerabilities.Title: ffmpeg: FFmpeg: Information disclosure and denial of service via out-of-bounds read in S/PDIF muxer
Vulnerabilities.Description: FFmpeg versions 0.7.1 through 8.1.2 contain an out-of-bounds read vulnerability in the S/PDIF muxer that allows attackers to access memory beyond buffer boundaries by supplying a crafted DTS stream with a core_size value larger than the actual packet length. Attackers can exploit the missing bounds check in the spdif_header_dts4 function by providing a malicious DTS-HD audio stream during S/PDIF re-muxing to trigger unauthorized memory reads beyond the packet buffer.

Vulnerabilities.Title: FFmpeg: Denial of Service via crafted RTP/ASF stream
Vulnerabilities.Description: FFmpeg versions 0.6.3 through 8.1.2 contain an infinite loop vulnerability in the RTP/ASF demuxer within libavformat/rtpdec_asf.c that allows remote attackers to cause denial of service by sending a crafted RTP/ASF stream. The rtp_asf_fix_header function fails to validate a minimum chunksize when iterating over ASF objects, causing the loop pointer to never advance when a chunksize is smaller than the 24-byte minimum ASF object header size, resulting in CPU exhaustion that denies service to legitimate users.

Vulnerabilities.Title: FFmpeg: FFmpeg: Arbitrary code execution, information disclosure, or denial of service via crafted ADX/AAX audio files
Vulnerabilities.Description: FFmpeg versions 4.4 through 8.1.2 contain an out-of-bounds memory access vulnerability in the ADX audio decoder within libavcodec/adxdec.c that allows attackers to trigger both out-of-bounds reads and writes by supplying a crafted ADX or AAX audio file with a mid-stream channel layout change. When AV_PKT_DATA_NEW_EXTRADATA side data is received mid-stream, the adx_decode_frame function re-parses the stream header but fails to update the internal channel state, causing subsequent decoding operations to access the prev[] state array using a stale channel count.

Vulnerabilities.Title: ffmpeg: FFmpeg: Arbitrary code execution via crafted video in vf_hqdn3d filter
Vulnerabilities.Description: FFmpeg through 8.1.2, fixed in commit 5d7112c, contains a heap out-of-bounds write vulnerability in the vf_hqdn3d filter that allows attackers to corrupt heap memory by supplying a crafted video whose frame resolution increases between frames when filtergraph reinitialization is disabled via the -reinit_filter 0 option. Attackers can provide a malicious video input where vf_hqdn3d.config_input() allocates undersized per-plane line-history buffers based on the initial frame width, and subsequent larger frames cause denoise_spatial() to write beyond the allocation boundary, resulting in heap memory corruption.

Vulnerabilities.Title: ffmpeg: FFmpeg: Arbitrary code execution via crafted CAF file
Vulnerabilities.Description: FFmpeg through 8.1.2, fixed in commit aafb5c6, contains a signed integer overflow vulnerability in the MACE6 audio decoder that allows attackers to corrupt heap memory by supplying a crafted CAF file with a malicious bytes_per_packet value. Attackers can craft a CAF file with oversized bytes_per_packet and frames_per_packet values in the desc chunk to trigger an integer overflow in mace_decode_frame() during output sample count computation, resulting in an undersized buffer allocation and heap out-of-bounds write that could enable code execution.

Vulnerabilities.Title: ffmpeg: FFmpeg: Arbitrary code execution via crafted PNG image
Vulnerabilities.Description: FFmpeg through 8.1.2, fixed in commit b506faf, contains a heap out-of-bounds write vulnerability in the native PNG and APNG encoders that allows remote attackers to corrupt heap memory by supplying a crafted PNG image with a malicious eXIf chunk. Attackers can craft an eXIf chunk where multiple IFD entries reference the same large value payload, causing canonical serialization to expand the output far beyond the undersized allocation estimated by add_exif_profile_size(), resulting in png_write_chunk() writing tens of thousands of bytes past the buffer boundary, leading to deterministic heap corruption, process crash, and potentially arbitrary code execution.

Vulnerabilities.Title: ffmpeg: FFmpeg: Arbitrary code execution via crafted PGS/SUP subtitle file
Vulnerabilities.Description: FFmpeg 7.0 through 8.1.2, fixed in commit 4da9812, contains a heap out-of-bounds write vulnerability in the vf_quirc filter that allows an attacker to corrupt heap memory by supplying a crafted PGS/SUP subtitle file with mismatched frame dimensions. Attackers can provide a subtitle file whose second presentation has larger dimensions than its first, causing av_image_copy_plane() to copy data exceeding the initial allocation size into the undersized libquirc grayscale image buffer, resulting in heap corruption and process crash with potential for code execution.

Vulnerabilities.Title: ffmpeg: FFmpeg: Arbitrary code execution via crafted WTV file in DVB subtitle parser
Vulnerabilities.Description: FFmpeg versions from 0.5 up to, but not including, 9.0 contain a signed integer overflow vulnerability in the DVB subtitle parser in libavcodec/dvbsub_parser.c that allows attackers to trigger a heap buffer overflow by supplying a crafted WTV file. The overflow causes the bounds-check guard expression to wrap to INT_MIN, bypassing the PARSE_BUF_SIZE comparison and invoking memcpy() with attacker-controlled data into a heap buffer, resulting in an out-of-bounds heap write and potential memory corruption or code execution.

Vulnerabilities.Title: ffmpeg: FFmpeg: Arbitrary Code Execution in CFHD Decoder via Crafted AVI File
Vulnerabilities.Description: FFmpeg versions from 4.4 up to, but not including, 9.0 contain an out-of-bounds heap write vulnerability in the native GoPro CineForm HD (CFHD) decoder that allows remote attackers to corrupt heap memory by supplying a crafted AVI file during stream probing. The cfhd_decode() function fails to enforce the non-Bayer logical output-width invariant in the transform-type-2 reconstruction path, causing horiz_filter_clip() to write oversized 16-bit sample rows far beyond the allocated output frame buffer, which can be escalated to arbitrary code execution via overwrite of a live cleanup callback pointer.

Vulnerabilities.Title: ffmpeg: FFmpeg: Heap buffer overflow via crafted HEVC input file during muxing
Vulnerabilities.Description: FFmpeg before commit acf5d7c contains a heap buffer overflow in the hvcC box writer. When writing an HEVC configuration record with more NAL units of a single type than the count field can represent, the NAL unit count overflows, causing a heap buffer overflow. A crafted HEVC input file triggers the overflow during muxing.

Vulnerabilities.Title: ffmpeg: FFmpeg: Stack Buffer Overflow in MPEG-PS Muxer
Vulnerabilities.Description: FFmpeg before commit 9d786e4 contains a stack buffer overflow in the MPEG-PS muxer (libavformat/mpegenc.c). When muxing input with more streams than the muxer's fixed-size stack buffer accommodates, the buffer is overflowed. A crafted input with an excessive number of streams triggers the overflow during MPEG-PS muxing.

Vulnerabilities.Title: ffmpeg: FFmpeg Heap Buffer Overflow via RIST Protocol Reader
Vulnerabilities.Description: FFmpeg before commit 1c10bcc contains a heap buffer overflow in the RIST protocol reader (libavformat/librist.c). librist_read() ignored its size argument and copied the full received payload length into the caller-provided destination buffer, overflowing it when the payload exceeds the destination size. This is reachable via the async:rist:// URL scheme, where the async wrapper supplies a smaller buffer than the received payload. A remote RIST sender can trigger the overflow by sending a packet whose payload exceeds the caller buffer size.

Vulnerabilities.Title: ffmpeg: FFmpeg: Memory corruption via crafted Dirac data unit
Vulnerabilities.Description: FFmpeg before commit 1cdeb3c contains a heap buffer overflow vulnerability in the VC-2/Dirac RTP packetizer (libavformat/rtpenc_vc2hq.c) that allows attackers to trigger memory corruption by supplying a crafted Dirac data unit. The packetizer copies an input-derived data unit or fragment size into a fixed-size buffer without an upper bound check, causing a heap buffer overflow when the crafted input is packetized for RTP output.

Vulnerabilities.Title: ffmpeg: FFmpeg: Information disclosure and denial of service via out-of-bounds read in DASH demuxer
Vulnerabilities.Description: FFmpeg before commit 65b0dab contains an out-of-bounds read in the DASH demuxer (libavformat/dashdec.c). When a live DASH manifest is refreshed with a startNumber that is lower than the previous value, the current sequence number is driven negative. The fragment retrieval function checked only the upper bound before indexing the fragments array, allowing a negative index to be used and causing an out-of-bounds read. A malicious or misconfigured DASH server can trigger this by serving a live manifest with a decreasing startNumber across a manifest refresh.

Vulnerabilities.Title: ffmpeg: ffmpeg: Information disclosure via missing SFTP host key verification
Vulnerabilities.Description: FFmpeg through 9.0.2 contains a missing host key verification vulnerability in the libssh-based sftp protocol handler that allows network attackers to impersonate SFTP servers. Attackers performing man-in-the-middle, DNS, or ARP spoofing can capture passwords supplied in sftp URLs, serve forged media, or receive uploaded output.

Vulnerabilities.Title: ffmpeg: ffmpeg: Denial of Service via empty SegmentTemplate in DASH demuxer
Vulnerabilities.Description: FFmpeg through 9.0.2 contains a denial of service vulnerability in the DASH demuxer that allows attackers to trigger an infinite loop by supplying an empty SegmentTemplate media URL. Attackers can craft an .mpd manifest declaring SegmentTemplate media="" so get_current_fragment() calls av_strireplace() with an empty search string, consuming CPU indefinitely.

Vulnerabilities.Title: ffmpeg: ffmpeg: Denial of Service via stack exhaustion from crafted MP4 files
Vulnerabilities.Description: FFmpeg through 9.0.2 contains a stack exhaustion vulnerability in av_encryption_init_info_free() in libavutil/encryption_info.c, which recursively frees AVEncryptionInitInfo linked lists built by the MOV demuxer's mov_read_pssh(). Attackers can supply a crafted MP4 file with tens of thousands of small pssh boxes to exhaust the stack and crash the process, while also causing quadratic CPU consumption.

Vulnerabilities.Title: ffmpeg: ffmpeg: Denial of Service via crafted HLS playlist
Vulnerabilities.Description: FFmpeg before 8.1.3 contains an infinite loop vulnerability in the HLS demuxer that allows remote attackers to cause denial of service because parse_playlist() accepts Master Playlist tags inside Media Playlists. Attackers can trick victims into opening a crafted self-referencing playlist that endlessly adds variants in hls_read_header(), causing unbounded CPU and I/O consumption.

Vulnerabilities.Title: ffmpeg: ffmpeg: Denial of Service via unlimited RTSP redirects
Vulnerabilities.Description: FFmpeg through 9.0.2 contains an infinite loop vulnerability in ff_rtsp_connect() in libavformat/rtsp.c that follows RTSP 3xx redirects without any redirect limit. Attackers controlling an RTSP server can answer every request with a 302 redirect to itself or another server, causing endless reconnects that saturate a CPU core.

Vulnerabilities.Title: ffmpeg: ffmpeg: Security restriction bypass via crafted HLS master playlist
Vulnerabilities.Description: FFmpeg before 8.1.3 contains a protection mechanism failure in the HLS demuxer that allows attackers to bypass protocol and allowed_extensions restrictions when opening child playlists. Attackers can supply a crafted master playlist whose child playlists use disallowed protocols or non-multimedia local files, making parse_playlist() open resources the HLS security policy should block.

Vulnerabilities.Title: ffmpeg: ffmpeg: Information disclosure via path traversal in IMF demuxer
Vulnerabilities.Description: FFmpeg 5.0 through 9.0.2 contains a path traversal vulnerability in the IMF demuxer that allows attackers to open files outside the package via unvalidated ASSETMAP Path elements. Attackers can supply a crafted IMF package with '..' or absolute paths to demux local MXF files, probe file existence and size, or trigger server-side requests.

Vulnerabilities.Title: ffmpeg: ffmpeg: information disclosure via crafted Go2Meeting stream
Vulnerabilities.Description: FFmpeg 2.0 through 9.0.2 contains a use of uninitialized variable vulnerability in the Go2Meeting decoder that allows attackers to leak stack memory through out-of-range palette indices. Attackers can craft a G2M3/G2M4 stream with a short Kempf palette so kempf_restore_buf() copies uninitialized stack bytes, including pointers or stack guards, into decoded output.

Vulnerabilities.Title: ffmpeg: ffmpeg: Information disclosure via truncated PCX image
Vulnerabilities.Description: FFmpeg 2.1 through 9.0.2 contains an uninitialized memory disclosure vulnerability in pcx_decode_frame() in libavcodec/pcx.c that leaves scanline buffer bytes uncleared when input ends early. Attackers can supply a crafted truncated RLE-compressed or uncompressed PCX image to leak heap memory contents through the decoded pixels.

Vulnerabilities.Title: ffmpeg: ffmpeg: Information disclosure via crafted Sun Raster image
Vulnerabilities.Description: FFmpeg 0.10 through 9.0.2 contains an uninitialized memory disclosure vulnerability in sunrast_decode_frame() in libavcodec/sunrast.c that leaves decoded image regions unwritten for truncated input. Attackers can supply a crafted truncated Sun Raster image, RLE-encoded or raw, to leak stale heap contents such as allocator metadata through the decoded picture.

Vulnerabilities.Title: ffmpeg: ffmpeg: Information disclosure via uninitialized palette entries in CDXL decoder
Vulnerabilities.Description: FFmpeg 4.4 through 9.0.2 contains a use of uninitialized variable vulnerability in the CDXL decoder that leaks stack memory into decoded pixels via unfilled HAM palette entries. Attackers can craft a type-0 CDXL file whose HAM pixels select unfilled new_palette entries in cdxl_decode_ham8() or cdxl_decode_ham6(), exposing stack bytes and pointer fragments in the BGR24 output.

Vulnerabilities.Title: ffmpeg: ffmpeg: Information disclosure via uninitialized heap memory in Huffyuv decoder
Vulnerabilities.Description: FFmpeg 2.3 through 9.0.2 contains a use of uninitialized resource vulnerability in the Huffyuv decoder that allows attackers to leak heap memory into decoded pixels via short packed-BGR bitstreams. Attackers can craft a Huffyuv BGR24/BGRA video whose entropy data ends early, causing decode_slice() to add uninitialized s->temp[0] bytes into output frames, exposing heap contents.

Vulnerabilities.Title: ffmpeg: ffmpeg: Denial of Service via NULL pointer dereference in G.726 decoder
Vulnerabilities.Description: FFmpeg through 9.0.2 contains a NULL pointer dereference vulnerability in g726_decode_frame() in libavcodec/g726.c because it ignores init_get_bits() failure on oversized packets. Attackers can supply a crafted AVI file with a 268435392-byte G.726 audio chunk to make the decoder read from a NULL buffer, crashing the process.

Vulnerabilities.Title: ffmpeg: ffmpeg: Denial of Service via crafted Electronic Arts TGV file
Vulnerabilities.Description: FFmpeg through 9.0.2 contains a NULL pointer dereference vulnerability in tgv_decode_inter() in libavcodec/eatgv.c that ignores init_get_bits() failure on oversized packets. Attackers can supply a crafted EA file with a kVGT frame followed by an fVGT inter frame with a 2^28-byte compressed block section, crashing the process for denial of service.

Vulnerabilities.Title: ffmpeg: ffmpeg: Denial of Service via crafted CLJR video frame
Vulnerabilities.Description: FFmpeg through 9.0.2 contains a NULL pointer dereference vulnerability in the Cirrus Logic AccuPak (CLJR) decoder in libavcodec/cljrdec.c because decode_frame() ignores init_get_bits() failure. Attackers can supply a crafted AVI file with a 2^28-byte CLJR frame that overflows the bit count, causing reads from a NULL buffer and crashing the process.

Vulnerabilities.Title: ffmpeg: ffmpeg: Denial of Service via crafted video frame in VBLE decoder
Vulnerabilities.Description: FFmpeg through 9.0.2 contains a NULL pointer dereference vulnerability in vble_decode_frame() in libavcodec/vble.c because it ignores init_get_bits() failure on oversized packets. Attackers can supply a crafted AVI file with a 268435452-byte VBLE frame, causing reads from a NULL bit reader buffer that crash the process.

Vulnerabilities.Title: ffmpeg: ffmpeg: Denial of Service via crafted Bink video file
Vulnerabilities.Description: FFmpeg through 9.0.2 contains a NULL pointer dereference vulnerability in the Bink video decoder because decode_frame() in libavcodec/bink.c ignores init_get_bits() failure. Attackers can supply a crafted Bink file with a frame of about 2^28 bytes, overflowing the bit count and crashing the process for denial of service.

Vulnerabilities.Title: ffmpeg: ffmpeg: Denial of Service via NULL pointer dereference in Motion Pixels decoder
Vulnerabilities.Description: FFmpeg through 9.0.2 contains a NULL pointer dereference vulnerability in the Motion Pixels decoder because mp_decode_frame() ignores init_get_bits() failure. Attackers supplying a roughly 2^28-byte packet through the libavcodec API overflow the bit count, causing reads from a NULL buffer that crash the process.

Vulnerabilities.Title: ffmpeg: ffmpeg: Denial of Service via NULL pointer dereference in EA TQI decoder
Vulnerabilities.Description: FFmpeg through 9.0.2 contains a NULL pointer dereference vulnerability in tqi_decode_frame() in libavcodec/eatqi.c, which ignores init_get_bits() failure after an integer overflow. Attackers can supply a crafted EA file with a pIQT chunk carrying a 2^28-byte payload to crash the process, causing denial of service.

Vulnerabilities.Title: ffmpeg: ffmpeg: Denial of service via oversized JV video packets
Vulnerabilities.Description: FFmpeg through 9.0.2 contains a NULL pointer dereference vulnerability in libavcodec/jvdec.c that allows attackers to crash applications by supplying oversized JV video packets. Attackers can pass a roughly 268435460-byte packet through the libavcodec API, overflowing the bit count so decode_frame() reads from a NULL buffer and causes denial of service.

Vulnerabilities.Title: ffmpeg: ffmpeg: Denial of Service via oversized packet in MPEG audio decoder
Vulnerabilities.Description: FFmpeg through 9.0.2 contains a NULL pointer dereference vulnerability in mp_decode_frame() in libavcodec/mpegaudiodec_template.c because init_get_bits() failure is ignored after a signed integer overflow. Attackers can pass an oversized packet to the mp3adu decoder through the libavcodec API, causing reads through a NULL buffer that crash the process.

Vulnerabilities.Title: ffmpeg: infinite loop denial of service via IMC/IAC decoder
